construct: Lithium enters collecting-duct principal cells through the apical epithelial sodium channel ENaC. Intracellular lithium interferes with vasopressin-dependent signaling and reduces aquaporin-2 abundance, impairing urinary concentration. Amiloride blocks ENaC and reduces lithium entry, making it mechanistically useful in lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Lithium-associated nephrogenic DI with a treatment chosen specifically to reduce lithium entry into collecting-duct principal cells points to amiloride blockade of apical ENaC.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Thiazides can reduce polyuria in nephrogenic DI, but they inhibit NCC and do not directly prevent lithium entry into principal cells.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The lead's direct-transporter wording and principal-cell lithium-entry clue isolate ENaC.
